methodological_questions: unit of analysis for player impact

historical_evidence.finding: Team offensive association structure is more similar to itself across split halves than to other teams, even after residualizing play-type rates. [APPS-080] Gate: C1 8/8 p<0.05; C2 S=0.319 perm_p=0.0002; C3 R2=0.080 PASS. Full: frobenius P1a S=0.352 p=0.0000 CI[0.327,0.378]; P1b S=0.353 CI[0.329,0.379]; cosine P1a 0.155 / P1b 0.144. residual_R2=0.043.

Structural influence is not reducible to usage and the usage-residual is a reproducible player property. [APPA-039] F1a cosine R2=0.094, residual-share=0.906, CI [0.768, 0.962] PASS; Frobenius R2=0.073 share=0.927 CI [0.828, 0.965]. F1b pooled-residual rho=+0.685 p=0.0000 CI [+0.649, +0.721]; usage-partial rho=+0.557 p=0.00

Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence. Unmatched conn vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched vs role: paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09 n=96. Vs terminal: +0.0777 t=2.37 p=0.0261 n=25.

Real player absences move the association structure (V1) and the LOO simulation predicts the magnitude (V2). [APPA-006] Gate G2 21/23 (91%) above null median; V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) mean(D_real - median_null)=+0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]. [APPA-007] Gate G3 Spearman +0.099. V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115, CI [-0.262, +0.615] FAIL.

Real on/off absence of a shaper displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper, and LOO L(p) tracks observed D_A. Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9, shaper larger in 81% of pairs; Delta D_pi=+0.011 p~1e-4; r(L,D_A)=+0.60 (shapers +0.79)

Conceding a PUTBACK causally suppresses the next offensive possession after matching on game state. TEAM ATT=-0.0038 CI[-0.025,+0.015] perm p=0.890 n_t=15614. STAR ATT=+0.0040 [-0.049,+0.052] p=0.834 n_t=2481. STAR Q4 ATT=-0.1045 [-0.217,+0.010] p=0.032 (gradient does not survive matching as a FINDING).
Connectors show larger on/off D_A than usage-matched terminal scorers. Delta=+0.078, p~0.026

Connector presence shields stars (higher TS, lower TO) and lifts lineup ORtg beyond talent. Star dTS +0.05 pp p=0.937; dTO +0.74 pp p=0.00364 (wrong sign for shielding). Star-init TO~HasConn beta=+0.34 pp p=0.439. HasConn on-off PPP BOTH_NULL (mean -0.041 p=0.939, median +0.528 p=0.731, n=73). Frequent-conn lin [cut; read_family for the full text]

Defenders who displace the opponent's initiation fingerprint (high D_A) also suppress opponent PPP. eligible 653/882; corr(D_A, n_on) all=-0.475 vs eligible=-0.036; eligible median D_A=0.0529, median dPPP_allowed=-0.298; corr(D_A, dPPP_allowed)=+0.020; quadrants ~161-166 each

failed_approaches.what_failed: LOO simulation predicting the magnitude of offensive association structure movement due to real player absences (V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115, CI [-0.262, +0.615] FAIL).
Conceding a PUTBACK causally suppressing the next offensive possession.
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw); original finding was a score/context confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector presence shielding stars (higher TS, lower TO) and lifting lineup ORtg beyond talent.
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null (adequately powered null result); PPP/TS/eFG shielding null; TO rate rises with connectors. Lineup ORtg lift is a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT; swap p=0.565).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Correlation between defensive D_A and dPPP_allowed.
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null (adequately powered null result); corr(D_A, dPPP_allowed)=+0.020 among 653 eligible.

evidence_establishes: Team offensive identity (association structure/fingerprint, measured as D_A) is a stable and reproducible concept (FAM:SF17, FAM:SF18).
Player absences, particularly of 'connectors' or 'shapers', cause measurable displacement of team offensive identity (D_A) (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF20, FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-PAP-028).
The Leave-One-Out (LOO) simulation (L) can track observed D_A to some extent (r(L,D_A)=+0.60 for shapers) (FAM:SF-PAP-014), though earlier work failed to predict its magnitude (FAM:SF20).
Direct on/off comparisons for 'connector' presence show a null effect on team Points Per Possession (PPP) (FAM:SF-APPS-087).
There is no correlation between defensive D_A (opponent's fingerprint displacement) and opponent PPP allowed (FAM:SF-PAP-030).
Confounding is a significant risk when attempting to establish causal links between events and offensive performance (FAM:SF-APPS-041).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the *magnitude* of offensive reorganization (D_A relative to L) predicts the *change* in points per possession.
The specific causal pathway or mechanism by which offensive reorganization might lead to changes in PPP, beyond the observed null effect of connector presence.
The reliability of D_A measurement in all contexts, given FAM:SF18 noted low measurement reliability as a limitation/risk.
own_inferences: The research question implies that 'offensive reorganization (relative to L)' is a measurable quantity, likely referring to D_A and its deviation from an LOO prediction.
The question is asking for a predictive relationship between a measure of structural change (D_A, potentially adjusted by L) and a performance outcome (change in PPP).

The historical evidence suggests that while reorganization (D_A) is a real phenomenon caused by player absence, the direct link between 'connector presence' and PPP is null, and a similar null result was found for defensive D_A and opponent PPP. This raises significant doubt about a positive relationship for offensive D_A and offensive PPP.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'reorganization (relative to L)' as intended by the question. It could mean D_A, or D_A - L, or (D_A - L) / L, etc. Different formulations might have different predictive power.
The specific type of player absence (e.g., 'connector', 'shaper') that induces the reorganization, and whether the observed null PPP effect for 'connectors' generalizes to all reorganizations.

historical_effect.explanation: Initially, the question seemed plausible given that offensive reorganization (D_A) is a well-established concept. However, the historical evidence, particularly FAM:SF-APPS-087 and FAM:SF-PAP-030, directly tested the impact of 'connector presence' and 'defensive D_A' on PPP, respectively, and found null results. This strongly suggests that a direct predictive relationship between offensive reorganization (D_A) and change in PPP is unlikely to be supported. The evidence shifted the predicted outcome from potentially supported to likely rejected or untestable, leading to a decision not to proceed as originally posed due to the low probability of a meaningful finding.

blocking_constraints.text: Prior work (FAM:SF-APPS-087, FAM:SF-PAP-030) has already established null or very weak relationships between proxies for 'reorganization' (connector presence, defensive D_A) and PPP, suggesting a low base rate for the hypothesized effect.

Changes in PPP are highly susceptible to confounding factors (e.g., opponent strength, game state, other lineup changes, natural variation in shooting luck), as highlighted by FAM:SF-APPS-041. Isolating the effect of 'reorganization' will be challenging.
FAM:SF18 noted 'low measurement reliability' as a limitation for structural influence, which could apply to D_A or its 'relative to L' adjustment, making it difficult to detect a true signal.

prior_work.summary: Previous studies have established that player absences cause measurable offensive reorganization (D_A). However, direct tests of the impact of 'connector presence' on team PPP (FAM:SF-APPS-087) and 'defensive D_A' on opponent PPP (FAM:SF-PAP-030) have yielded null results. This indicates that while reorganization is real, its direct link to PPP changes is not supported by existing evidence, directly addressing a component of the current question.

risks.text: Given previous null findings for related concepts (connector presence on-off PPP, defensive D_A vs dPPP allowed), the true effect size might be very small or non-existent, leading to a high probability of a null result even if the hypothesis were true.

Changes in points per possession are influenced by many factors beyond offensive reorganization, such as opponent strength, game pace, other simultaneous lineup changes, and natural variance in shooting. Carefully controlling for these will be critical and difficult.

The measurement of 'offensive reorganization' (D_A) and its 'relative to L' component may suffer from reliability issues, as indicated by FAM:SF18, making it difficult to accurately capture the independent variable.

Detecting a small effect size, especially if the true effect is close to null, would require a very large sample of player absence events and corresponding reorganization measures, which might be limited by the available data, particularly for specific player types or magnitudes of reorganization.
The measure of 'reorganization' (D_A) might have a mechanical floor or ceiling, limiting its variance and thus its predictive power. Also, PPP has a natural floor/ceiling within a game context.

design.estimand: The causal effect of a unit change in offensive reorganization (measured as D_A, or D_A adjusted for LOO prediction L) on the subsequent change in team points per possession (PPP) in games following a key player's absence.
design.unit: Player absence spells, defined as a contiguous set of games where a designated 'shaper' or 'connector' player (as defined by prior work) is absent from the lineup, compared to a baseline period (e.g., 10 games prior to absence).
design.sample: All player absence spells for 'shaper' or 'connector' players in the NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons where the player missed at least 3 consecutive games. Minimum 148 spells and n=986 games for PPP calculations (as per data availability).
design.power: The available sample size (n=148 spells) is likely insufficient to detect a small effect size, especially given previous null results. A power analysis would be required but is not expected to yield a positive result for a meaningful effect size. The study would likely be underpowered to detect anything but a large effect.
design.controls: Matched control design (if proceeding): Match absence spells based on opponent strength (e.g., Elo rating), game pace, home/away status, and presence/absence of other key players. Regression with fixed effects for team and season, and covariates for opponent strength, game state (score margin, time remaining), and other lineup changes. Change in PPP would be calculated as the difference between PPP during absence and PPP in a baseline period, or compared to matched control games.
design.falsification: A strong falsification would involve demonstrating that the observed 'reorganization' (D_A) is merely a consequence of other unmeasured factors that also drive PPP changes, or that the measurement of D_A is unreliable or sensitive to noise. The primary falsification would be a null finding, consistent with prior work.
design.multiplicity: No multiple testing planned for the primary hypothesis. If secondary analyses were considered (e.g., by player role, magnitude of D_A), appropriate adjustments for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, FDR) would be applied.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null hypothesis (no predictive relationship) if the p-value for the primary estimand is less than 0.05. Given the historical evidence, a p-value > 0.05 would be interpreted as a powered null, supporting the rejection of the hypothesis.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, and partial 2025-26 regular season and playoffs (as of 2026-11-01).

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
